BLOCKED ON HELPER_MISSING after recon; no package was written and the gate was not run (0 gate runs). The card's RosDriver cannot express this runtime and no SDK family helper covers its actual Drake/LCM interface.

WHAT THE UPSTREAM IS: a simulation/control research stack plus a fixed demo script, not an installable environment or device. README.md:3 says it 'contains code for the simulation and control of quadruped robots using [Drake]'. README.md:21-27 gives only a CMake build ('Compile C++ code (includes TOWR and custom LCM bindings...)'; cmake; make), and README.md:29-33 the run path ('Start the drake visualizer'; 'Run the simulation script ./simulate.py'). The root CMakeLists.txt:1-4 only declares the project and add_subdirectory(towr); there is no root package.xml, setup.py, pyproject.toml or requirements.txt, and the card's install block is empty. The only package.xml files belong to third-party code included in the tree: towr/package.xml:1-33 describes the TOWR C++ trajectory-optimization library and models/anymal_b_simple_description/package.xml:1-19 a catkin/roslaunch model description. They are not a node or endpoint of this repository.

NO ENTRY CLASS / ENVIRONMENT: simulate.py is 213 lines of top-level script code with no class or function definition; it imports pydrake.all at :3, fixes use_lcm=False at :11, selects one planner and controller at :13-18 and :98-118, builds the diagram at :36-149, creates a Simulator at :160, sets q0/qd0 at :171-179, and calls simulator.AdvanceTo(sim_time) at :182 with sim_time=6.0 at :20. Importing it would execute that demo. A text search of the owned Python finds no gym/gymnasium Env, no def step and no def reset; the only simulator advance is simulate.py:182. Thus GymnasiumDriver has no env/action space to bind and a direct Driver has no class that owns the simulation. The card's hints resolve to generated codecs, not device entries: robot_state_control_lcmt.decode at lcm_types/cheetahlcm/robot_state_control_lcmt.py:35 and trunk_state_t.decode at lcm_types/trunklcm/trunk_state_t.py:81.

THE ACTUAL RUNTIME IS OPTIONAL LCM INSIDE A CONTROLLER, NOT A DEVICE API: BasicController is a Drake LeafSystem (controllers/basic_controller.py:8) constructed with a plant and context (:21-30); with use_lcm=True it subscribes to 'robot_current_state' (:55-61), decodes robot_state_control_lcmt (:79-87), and publishes robot_state_control_lcmt on 'robot_control_input' (:286-317), with u clipped to [-150,150] at :350. TowrTrunkPlanner subscribes to 'trunk_state' (planners/towr.py:19-21), decodes trunk_state_t (:37-49), and GenerateTrunkTrajectory launches the compiled build/towr/trunk_mpc binary and blocks in while not self.traj_finished: self.lc.handle() (:50-68). Both are components inside simulate.py; neither exposes an environment reset/step, an external device lifecycle, or a stop.

WHY EACH HELPER FAILS: RosDriver is a configuration-only rosbridge driver (MHS/sdk/docs/ros-driver.md:5-9). The clone has no ROS node, service, action, .msg, .srv or .launch file and no rospy/rclpy import (the 'ROS' markers are the third-party package.xml files above). Declaring endpoints/types would invent them. GymnasiumDriver needs an Env with action_space/reset/step; none exists. MujocoDriver is for MuJoCo, not Drake. PythonObjectDriver cannot wrap a simulation class because none exists. A direct Driver would have to write a new LCM transport and environment wrapper around top-level script code, and its fake would then supply the step, action space and stop the upstream does not define; that is forbidden by the task rules. The upstream-sim mock path has no runnable API: simulate.py:182 is a fixed 6 s script and TOWR needs build/towr/trunk_mpc.

NO GENUINE STOP: a search of the owned Python for stop/estop/halt/pause/abort/safe finds only the planner comment 'we can stop listening to LCM' at planners/towr.py:48. There is no stop, pause, reset or e-stop method/service/action. A zero-torque publication is transmission-only and is not an acknowledged stop; the runtime would have only a software latch with no native effect, so no safe state can be claimed. The card's R0 simulated floor does not create a stop where the native has none.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: none possible; the card's family/helper and every alternate shape lack a concrete upstream entry and an acknowledged stop. The registry's own integration record for this package records NO_ENTRY_SYMBOL and NO_INSTALL_FILE (MHS/registry/repos/robots/vincekurtz__quadruped_drake.json). I report HELPER_MISSING rather than ENTRY_UNVERIFIED because the card names no entry symbol and the blocker is the missing Drake/LCM/environment helper, not an existing symbol that could not be found. The repository is a simulator/control stack rather than a packaged device, but because the card plans a sim-env and the concrete gap is the missing Drake/LCM helper, HELPER_MISSING is reported rather than NOT_A_DEVICE. No hardware was attached; no upstream code was imported, run or installed; no network or pip install was used; the clone at 2b0ba8449b99e0c6ba1379e176f7217bcd6de275 is unchanged (git status clean).

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Confirmed the author's recon block (no package written): the pinned repository is a Drake/LCM quadruped simulation and control stack whose only run path is the top-level script simulate.py (use_lcm = False at :11, Simulator at :160, a fixed AdvanceTo(6.0) at :182), with no class or function that owns the simulation, no Gym-style step/reset, no ROS node, launch, msg or srv file and no rospy/rclpy import outside the vendored TOWR tree; the card's ROS family comes from the vendored towr/package.xml and models/anymal_b_simple_description/package.xml, the card's hints are generated LCM codecs, the planner launches build/towr/trunk_mpc and blocks in an LCM handle loop without a timeout (planners/towr.py:50-68), the controller clips u to [-150, 150] (basic_controller.py:350), and nothing offers a stop. The registry's drake family has no helper planned, so HELPER_MISSING stands; the override proposal records skip as sim-env, as for ardupilot_gazebo. The reviewer changed no file; the gate fails G1, G2, G3 and G9 because the directory holds only task.json and RESULT.json, and it wrote no check-report.json. For the human reviewer: Simulation only; no hardware path in the clone. Wrapping it would need a new Drake environment around top-level script code plus an LCM transport, and TOWR planning spawns a compiled binary and waits on LCM without a timeout.
